name: George Town
tagline: The capital, the port and the financial district
description: The working centre of the Cayman Islands, holding the government, the funds and insurance industry, the cruise terminal and the National Museum. It is busy on ship days and quiet otherwise, and it is where the island's professional life happens.
bestFor: Anyone working in the financial sector or needing government offices
pros: The whole professional network is here
Eden Rock and Devil's Grotto shore diving from the waterfront

name: Seven Mile Beach
tagline: The strip everyone means when they say Grand Cayman
description: A continuous run of condominiums, hotels and restaurants along what is actually about ten kilometres of white sand on the island's western side. It is the most expensive address in the Cayman Islands and the beach genuinely is as good as its reputation.
bestFor: Anyone whose priority is the beach and who has the budget for it
pros: One of the best beaches in the Caribbean
Restaurants and bars along the whole strip
Public access is protected along the sand
cons: The most expensive rents on the island
West Bay Road traffic at peak

name: Camana Bay
tagline: The purpose-built town centre behind the beach
description: A planned mixed-use district developed since 2007 between Seven Mile Beach and the North Sound, with offices, apartments, a cinema, a good bookshop and an observation tower. It is the closest thing the island has to a walkable town centre and it was designed to be.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to work, shop and eat without driving
pros: Genuinely walkable with everything on site
Best coworking and office space on the island
Farmers market and a good cinema
cons: Beach is a walk away rather than at the door

name: West Bay
tagline: The old district at the northern end
description: The residential district at the top of the island, home to much of the Caymanian population, with Hell's limestone formations, the turtle centre and the quieter northern end of Seven Mile Beach. It is more local than anywhere else on Grand Cayman.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a real neighbourhood rather than a resort strip
pros: More affordable than the beach strip
Northwest Point and the reef nearby
cons: Needs a car for most things
Traffic into George Town at peak

name: East End
tagline: The undeveloped side, with the blowholes
description: The far eastern district, sparsely built and facing the windward coast, with blowholes along the ironshore, the wreck of the Ten Sail and some of the best and least crowded diving on the island. Life here runs at a different speed from the west.
bestFor: Divers and anyone who wants the island without the crowd
pros: The cheapest housing on Grand Cayman
